rules.description: A supplier is liable to register in the State/UT from where it makes a taxable supply if its aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds the applicable limit (Rs 20 lakh; Rs 10 lakh in Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura; Rs 40 lakh for exclusive supply of goods where Notification 10/2019-CT applies).
rules.notes: "Taxable" here includes nil-rated supplies: the handbook (p. 18, PDF 24) says a person dealing in nil-rated supplies is not covered by s.23(1) and is liable to register. Aggregate turnover includes exempt supplies, exports and inter-State supplies to distinct persons, and excludes RCM inward supplies and taxes (p. 9-13).
rules.legal_basis: s.22(1) CGST Act, with provisos and Notification 10/2019-CT
rules.plain_language: Your yearly turnover is above the GST registration limit for your State and type of business.
rules.ca_question: What is the aggregate turnover (s.2(6), all-India, PAN level) for the financial year, and from which States are taxable supplies made?

rules.description: Where a business carried on by a registered person is transferred as a going concern (succession or otherwise), the transferee or successor is liable to register from the date of transfer.
rules.plain_language: You are taking over a GST-registered business as a going concern.
rules.ca_question: Is the client the transferee or successor of a registered person's business taken over as a going concern?

rules.description: On transfer under a scheme of amalgamation or demerger sanctioned by a High Court, Tribunal or other authority, the transferee is liable to register from the date the Registrar of Companies issues the certificate of incorporation giving effect to the order, irrespective of threshold.
rules.plain_language: Your company receives a business under a sanctioned amalgamation or demerger.
rules.ca_question: Is the client the transferee in a sanctioned amalgamation or demerger?

rules.description: Persons making any inter-State taxable supply must register irrespective of turnover. Exports are inter-State supplies under the IGST Act, so exporters must register even though exports are zero-rated.
rules.plain_language: You sell to customers in another State or export, which requires registration whatever your turnover.
rules.ca_question: Does the client make any inter-State taxable supply, including exports?

rules.description: A casual taxable person (occasionally supplies in a State/UT where it has no fixed place of business) must register in that State/UT irrespective of threshold, at least 5 days before commencing business, with an advance deposit of estimated net tax liability.
rules.plain_language: You will supply occasionally in a State where you have no fixed place of business (for example an event or exhibition).
rules.ca_question: Will the client make occasional taxable supplies in a State/UT where it has no fixed place of business, and for how long?

rules.description: Where the occasional activity (long-running exhibition) exceeds 180 days the person cannot be treated as a casual taxable person and must obtain normal registration; the allotment or consent letter for the exhibition premises is proof of place of business and no advance tax is needed.
rules.notes: The circular says such a person "would be required to obtain registration as a normal taxable person". Whether this is a s.24 trigger or a s.22 liability in the exhibition State is not stated; modelled as compulsory. CA to confirm.
rules.plain_language: Your event or exhibition runs longer than 180 days, so you need a normal registration instead of a casual one.
rules.ca_question: Does the exhibition or occasional activity run for more than 180 days?

rules.description: Persons required to pay tax under reverse charge must register irrespective of threshold.
rules.notes: s.9(4) applies to specified registered recipients only, so an unregistered person cannot be liable under s.9(4). The questionnaire asks about s.9(3) liability; the CA should confirm the specific notified entry.
rules.plain_language: You must pay GST yourself on some purchases (reverse charge), which requires registration.
rules.ca_question: Is the client actually liable under a s.9(3) notification as an unregistered recipient? Several RCM entries apply only to registered recipients (handbook Illustration on renting by a local authority, p. 13).

rules.description: An e-commerce operator required to pay tax under s.9(5) (notified services: passenger transport, accommodation, housekeeping, restaurant services) must register irrespective of turnover.
rules.notes: From 1 Nov 2026 the revised REG-01 has a separate section for ECOs liable under s.9(5) (research, Advisory 681), so the route form detail changes on that date.
rules.legal_basis: s.24(iv); s.9(5) CGST Act; s.5(5) IGST Act
rules.plain_language: Your platform pays GST on behalf of service providers (rides, stays, housekeeping, food delivery).
rules.ca_question: Is the operator liable to pay tax under s.9(5) on any notified service?

rules.description: A non-resident taxable person making taxable supply in India must register irrespective of threshold, in FORM GST REG-09 at least 5 days before commencing business, with an advance deposit; registration is valid for up to 90 days.
rules.notes: An NRTP cannot opt for composition (handbook p. 26).
rules.legal_basis: s.24(v), s.2(77), s.27 CGST Act; Rule 13
rules.plain_language: You have no fixed place of business or residence in India but will supply here occasionally.
rules.ca_question: Does the client have any fixed place of business or residence in India?

rules.description: Departments or establishments of the Central or a State Government, local authorities, governmental agencies, and notified persons (authorities or boards with 51% or more Government equity or control, societies established by Government, PSUs) required to deduct tax under s.51 must register as TDS deductors irrespective of turnover, using TAN.
rules.notes: Deduction applies where the total value of supply under a contract exceeds Rs 2.5 lakh. Authorities under the Ministry of Defence other than those in Annexure A to Notification 50/2018-CT are carved out (handbook p. 28). Supplies between two s.51 persons are carved out.
rules.legal_basis: s.24(vi), s.51 CGST Act; Notification 50/2018-CT as amended
rules.plain_language: As a government body or PSU you must deduct GST TDS from supplier payments, which needs a TDS registration.
rules.ca_question: Is the client a person specified under s.51(1) or Notification 50/2018-CT? Note the Ministry of Defence carve-out.

rules.description: A registered person receiving supplies of metal scrap (Chapters 72 to 81 of the Customs Tariff) from another registered person is a notified TDS deductor and must register as such.
rules.notes: effective_from is the notification date (09.10.2024) given in the handbook; the handbook does not state the commencement date. EFFECTIVE DATE NOT VERIFIED.
rules.legal_basis: s.24(vi), s.51; Notification 50/2018-CT as amended by Notification 25/2024-CT dated 09.10.2024
rules.plain_language: You buy metal scrap from registered suppliers, so you must deduct GST TDS and register as a deductor.
rules.ca_question: Does the client, as a registered person, receive metal scrap of Chapters 72 to 81 from registered persons?

rules.description: From 1 Nov 2026, TDS registration under s.51 extends to recipients of used cooking oil, plastic scrap, tyre scrap and e-waste. Metal scrap remains under Notification 25/2024-CT.
rules.notes: Secondary source only (TaxGuru via research note). Notification text, conditions (whether the recipient and supplier must be registered) and HSN scope NOT VERIFIED.
rules.legal_basis: s.24(vi), s.51; Notification 07/2026-CT dated 27.10.2026 (per research note)
rules.plain_language: You buy used cooking oil, plastic scrap, tyre scrap or e-waste from registered suppliers, so you must register as a TDS deductor.
rules.ca_question: Which items does the client receive, and does Notification 07/2026-CT cover them (conditions not read)?

rules.description: A person making taxable supplies on behalf of other taxable persons as an agent must register irrespective of threshold. Per Circular 57/31/2018-GST, the test is whether the agent issues the invoice for the further supply in its own name (can pass title); the principal must be a taxable person and the supply must be taxable.
rules.notes: A pure facilitator (scenarios 1 and 2 of the circular) is not liable under s.24(vii) but is liable under s.22(1) if its own taxable services exceed the threshold.
rules.legal_basis: s.24(vii), s.2(5), Schedule I para 3; Circular 57/31/2018-GST
rules.plain_language: You sell goods for someone else and bill the customer in your own name.
rules.ca_question: Does the agent issue invoices in its own name for supplies on behalf of a principal who is a taxable person?

rules.description: An Input Service Distributor must take a separate ISD registration, whether or not separately registered; no threshold applies.
rules.notes: Research note: Circular 260 may cover ISD registrations (not read). See conflict C-004.
rules.plain_language: Your head office receives common service bills to pass the credit on to branches, which needs a separate ISD registration.
rules.ca_question: Does an office of the client receive input service invoices on behalf of distinct persons to distribute credit?

rules.description: Persons supplying goods or services (other than s.9(5) services) through an e-commerce operator required to collect TCS under s.52 must register irrespective of turnover, subject to the exemptions in Notifications 65/2017-CT (services) and 34/2023-CT (goods).
rules.plain_language: You sell through an online marketplace that collects TCS.
rules.ca_question: Does the client sell through an ECO that collects TCS, and are any of those supplies outside s.9(5)?

rules.description: Every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source under s.52 must register (FORM GST REG-07), irrespective of turnover.
rules.notes: TCS rate 0.5% (0.25% + 0.25%, or 0.5% IGST) per Notification 15/2024-CT (handbook p. 37).
rules.plain_language: Your marketplace collects payments for sellers and must collect TCS, which needs a TCS registration.
rules.ca_question: Does the operator collect consideration on behalf of suppliers so that s.52 TCS applies?

rules.description: Every person supplying OIDAR services from a place outside India to a person in India other than a registered person must register (single registration in FORM GST REG-10).
rules.notes: The OIDAR definition was widened w.e.f. 01.10.2023 (the "essentially automated" condition dropped). Where the recipient is registered, the recipient pays under reverse charge (no s.24(xi) liability on that account).
rules.legal_basis: s.24(xi) CGST Act; s.14 IGST Act; Rule 14
rules.plain_language: You sell digital services from outside India to consumers in India.
rules.ca_question: Are OIDAR services supplied from outside India to non-taxable online recipients in India?

rules.description: Every person supplying online money gaming from a place outside India to a person in India must register (FORM GST REG-10).
rules.plain_language: You offer online money gaming from outside India to players in India.
rules.ca_question: Does the client supply online money gaming (s.2(80B)) from outside India to persons in India?

rules.description: A person engaged exclusively in supplying goods or services that are not liable to tax or are wholly exempt is not liable to register. Nil-rated supplies do NOT qualify.
rules.notes: Since 1 Oct 2023 the handbook reads s.23 as overriding s.22 and s.24. A single taxable sale (e.g. of a capital asset) ends the exemption (Illustration 9).
rules.plain_language: Everything you supply is fully exempt from GST or outside GST (not merely 0%-rated), so you need not register.
rules.ca_question: Are ALL of the client's supplies wholly exempt or non-taxable (and none nil-rated or taxable, including sale of business assets)?

rules.description: An agriculturist (individual or HUF cultivating land by own or family labour or hired labour under personal supervision) is not liable to register to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land.
rules.notes: Any other supply brings the person back under s.22/s.24 (supplier-based and supply-based test).
rules.plain_language: You are a farmer (individual or HUF) selling only produce from your own cultivation.
rules.ca_question: Is the client an individual/HUF agriculturist supplying only produce out of cultivation of land, with no other supplies?

rules.description: Persons only engaged in making taxable supplies on which the whole tax is payable by the recipient under s.9(3) are exempt from registration (e.g. an advocate).
rules.notes: Superseded on 09.10.2024 by EX-N5-2017-RCM-ONLY-2024 (metal scrap carve-out).
rules.plain_language: All your sales are ones where the buyer pays the GST under reverse charge (for example legal services), so you need not register.
rules.ca_question: Is every outward supply one on which the recipient pays the entire tax under s.9(3)?

rules.description: As EX-N5-2017-RCM-ONLY, except that the exemption does not extend to persons supplying metal scrap of Chapters 72 to 81 of the Customs Tariff.
rules.notes: Commencement date of Notification 24/2024-CT not stated in the handbook; notification date used. EFFECTIVE DATE NOT VERIFIED.
rules.legal_basis: s.23(2); Notification 5/2017-CT as amended by Notification 24/2024-CT dated 09.10.2024
rules.plain_language: All your sales are ones where the buyer pays the GST under reverse charge, and you do not sell metal scrap, so you need not register.
rules.ca_question: Is every outward supply under s.9(3) reverse charge, and does the client supply any metal scrap of Chapters 72 to 81?

rules.description: Persons making inter-State taxable supplies of services only, with aggregate turnover (all-India) not exceeding Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh in Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura), are exempt from registration.
rules.legal_basis: s.23(2); Notification 10/2017-IT dated 13.10.2017 as amended by 3/2019-IT
rules.plain_language: You supply only services, and your turnover is under the limit, so selling services to other States does not by itself require registration.
rules.ca_question: Does the client supply services only, and is aggregate turnover within Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh for the four States)?

rules.description: A services-only supplier whose inter-State supplies include exports, with turnover within Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh). Notification 10/2017-IT on its face exempts inter-State suppliers of services; the handbook Illustration 6 says all exporters must register regardless of turnover.
rules.notes: See conflict C-014. Always routed to the CA.
rules.legal_basis: s.23(2); Notification 10/2017-IT as amended by 3/2019-IT, read against handbook Illustration 6
rules.plain_language: You export services and your turnover is under the limit; whether you must register depends on a point a CA should confirm.
rules.ca_question: Does Notification 10/2017-IT exempt this small exporter of services, or does the handbook position (Illustration 6, all exporters must register) apply?

rules.description: Persons making inter-State taxable supplies of notified handicraft goods (or products made by craftsmen predominantly by hand), with all-India aggregate turnover within the State threshold, holding PAN and generating e-way bills, are exempt from registration.
rules.notes: Product list is in Notification 21/2018-CT(Rate); not reproduced in the handbook beyond examples.
rules.plain_language: You make only hand-made / handicraft goods within the turnover limit, so inter-State sales do not by themselves require registration.
rules.ca_question: Are the inter-State supplies only of handicraft goods as defined in Notification 21/2018-CT(Rate), with PAN and e-way bills, within the threshold?

rules.description: Casual taxable persons making inter-State taxable supplies of notified handicraft goods (or hand-made products), within the State threshold, holding PAN and generating e-way bills, are exempt from registration.
rules.plain_language: You sell handicrafts at fairs in other States within the turnover limit, so a casual registration is not needed.
rules.ca_question: Are the casual supplies only of notified handicraft goods, with PAN and e-way bills, within the threshold?

rules.description: Job workers making inter-State supply of services to a registered person are exempt from obtaining registration, subject to conditions in the notification.
rules.notes: Conditions NOT VERIFIED; the engine routes any reliance on this exemption to the CA.
rules.legal_basis: s.23(2); Notification 7/2017-IT dated 14.09.2017 as amended by 2/2019-IT
rules.plain_language: Your only inter-State supplies are job-work services for registered businesses.
rules.ca_question: The handbook says this exemption is "subject to certain conditions" without listing them. Do the notification's conditions (and any carve-outs) apply to this job worker?

rules.description: Persons supplying services (other than s.9(5) services) through a TCS-collecting ECO, with aggregate turnover not exceeding Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh in special category States), are exempt.
rules.legal_basis: s.23(2); Notification 65/2017-CT dated 15.11.2017 as amended by 6/2019-CT
rules.plain_language: You provide services through an online platform and your turnover is under the limit, so the platform alone does not require you to register.
rules.ca_question: Is the client a services-only supplier through the ECO with aggregate turnover within Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh)?

rules.description: Persons supplying goods through an ECO are exempt if aggregate turnover in the preceding and the current financial year does not exceed the s.22(1) limit for the State, supplies are intra-State only, in one State/UT only, the person has PAN, has declared PAN, address and State on the portal and obtained an enrolment number (one per State/UT).
rules.notes: Notification date used; commencement date not stated in the handbook. EFFECTIVE DATE NOT VERIFIED.
rules.plain_language: You sell goods online within one State only, below the turnover limit, and have an enrolment number, so you need not register.
rules.ca_question: Are all seven conditions of Notification 34/2023-CT met (turnover in both years, intra-State only, one State, PAN, portal declaration, enrolment number)?

rules.description: A person supplying both goods and services through an ECO may fall under both exemptions. The handbook does not address the combined case.

source_ref.section: Combination of 1.5.9 goods and services exemptions; not addressed in handbook

rules.notes: Interpretive gap; always routed to the CA.
rules.plain_language: You sell both goods and services online below the limits; whether both exemptions apply together needs a CA's view.
rules.ca_question: Can Notifications 65/2017-CT and 34/2023-CT be applied together to a supplier of both goods and services through ECOs?

rules.description: A person engaged exclusively in supply of goods with aggregate turnover not exceeding Rs 40 lakh is exempt, except: s.24 persons; suppliers of ice cream and edible ice, pan masala, tobacco, fly-ash bricks/aggregates/blocks, bricks of fossil meals, building bricks, earthen or roofing tiles; intra-State suppliers in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Sikkim, Telangana, Tripura, Uttarakhand; voluntary registrants.
rules.notes: Used by the engine to pick the goods-only column of the threshold table; the State exclusion is already reflected in thresholds.yaml. The p. 9 summary lists only ice cream, pan masala and tobacco; the fuller list (bricks, tiles) is on p. 4. The date the bricks and tiles were added is not stated (NOT VERIFIED). Goods supplier with exempt interest income: see conflict C-006.
rules.plain_language: You supply only goods (none of the excluded items), so the higher Rs 40 lakh limit applies in your State.
rules.ca_question: Does the client supply only goods, none of them among the excluded items in Notification 10/2019-CT?

rules.description: A person not liable under s.22 or s.24 may register voluntarily, and is then treated like any other registered person (invoicing, returns, ITC).
rules.notes: A voluntary registrant loses the Notification 10/2019-CT Rs 40 lakh exemption (clause (d)). The engine does not treat "don't know" on this preference as a legal uncertainty; it adds an open question instead (design decision for CA sign-off).
rules.plain_language: You are not required to register, but you may choose to, for example to claim input tax credit or sell to GST-registered businesses.
rules.ca_question: Does the client want to register voluntarily (ITC, B2B customers), accepting full compliance obligations?

deadlines.description: A person liable under s.22 or s.24 (other than casual and non-resident taxable persons) must apply within 30 days from the date liability arises, in every State/UT where liable.
deadlines.notes: Persons making supply from territorial waters register in the coastal State/UT nearest the baseline, also within 30 days (row C); not asked in v1.
deadlines.plain_language: Apply within 30 days of the date you first become liable to register.
deadlines.legal_basis: s.25(1) CGST Act; handbook table 2.1 row A

deadlines.description: A casual or non-resident taxable person must apply at least 5 days before commencing business.
deadlines.plain_language: Apply at least 5 days before you start supplying.

deadlines.description: Registration of a casual or non-resident taxable person is valid for the period applied for or 90 days from the effective date, whichever is earlier; extendable once by up to 90 days on REG-11, filed before expiry, with an additional advance deposit.
deadlines.plain_language: The registration lasts up to 90 days and can be extended once by up to 90 more days.
deadlines.legal_basis: s.27(1), s.27(2) proviso CGST Act; Rule 15(1)

deadlines.description: Registration is effective from the date the person becomes liable if the application is made within 30 days of liability; otherwise from the date of grant.
deadlines.plain_language: If you apply within 30 days, your registration counts from the day you became liable; if later, only from the date it is granted.

deadlines.description: The transferee or successor is liable to register with effect from the date of transfer or succession.
deadlines.notes: The application time limit (30 days, s.25(1)) also applies.
deadlines.plain_language: Registration is required from the date you take over the business.

deadlines.description: The transferee is liable to register from the date the Registrar of Companies issues the certificate of incorporation giving effect to the amalgamation or demerger order.
deadlines.plain_language: Registration is required from the date the Registrar of Companies gives effect to the scheme.

routes.description: Rule 13 - REG-09, valid passport (and foreign tax ID for entities), advance deposit of estimated tax, authorised signatory resident in India with PAN.
routes.notes: Rule 9 applies mutatis mutandis to NRTP (Rule 13(3)).
routes.name: Non-resident taxable person registration
routes.plain_language: Apply on REG-09 with a self-attested passport copy, at least 5 days before starting, after paying an advance deposit of the estimated tax.

routes.description: Rule 14 - single REG-10 registration, administered by the Principal Commissioner of Central Tax, Bengaluru West.
routes.name: OIDAR / online money gaming supplier outside India
routes.plain_language: Apply once for all of India on REG-10, yourself or through an appointed agent in India.

routes.description: Rule 12 - REG-07 with TAN; Part A State of deduction, Part B State of principal place of business.
routes.notes: Scrap recipients are already registered persons; the REG-07 registration is in addition to their normal registration.
routes.name: TDS deductor registration (s.51)
routes.plain_language: Apply on REG-07 using TAN. Registration is usually granted within 3 working days.

routes.description: Rule 12 - REG-07 for ECOs required to collect tax under s.52.
routes.name: TCS collector registration (s.52, e-commerce operator)
routes.plain_language: Apply on REG-07 in each State where you collect TCS. Registration is usually granted within 3 working days.

routes.description: Rule 8(1), 8(6) - REG-01 with "casual taxable person = Yes", temporary reference number, advance deposit of estimated net tax liability (Circular 71/45/2018-GST).
routes.name: Casual taxable person registration
routes.plain_language: Apply on REG-01 as a casual taxable person, giving estimated supplies and net tax, and pay the advance deposit; the acknowledgement issues only after the deposit.

routes.description: REG-01 Part B, reason to obtain registration = Input Service Distributor only.
routes.notes: Rule 14A cannot be combined with "Input Service Distributor only" (GST portal user guide).
routes.name: Input Service Distributor registration
routes.plain_language: Apply on REG-01 choosing "Input Service Distributor only" as the reason. This is in addition to any normal registration.

routes.description: Separate registration for the SEZ unit/developer even if registered elsewhere in the same State; reason SEZ Unit / SEZ Developer with SEZ name, approval order, approving authority and validity period.
routes.notes: Whether an SEZ unit is liable at all is decided by s.22/s.24 like any other person.
routes.name: Separate registration for SEZ unit or developer
routes.plain_language: Your SEZ unit or developer activity needs its own registration, separate from your other places in the same State.

routes.description: Rule 14B (Notification 05/2026-CT): for a person with an active regular registration in another State under the same PAN, with no physical presence or regular registration in the target State, supplying there only through ECOs, within the output-tax cap; ECO consent and Aadhaar plus document verification required.
routes.notes: All conditions come from secondary sources; rule text not read.
routes.name: Rule 14B - registration for e-commerce sellers in another State
routes.plain_language: If you are already registered in another State and only sell into this State through marketplaces, Rule 14B offers a lighter registration.

conditions.fail_message: Applicant has not opted for Rule 14B.

conditions.description: Active regular registration in another State/UT under the same PAN.
conditions.fail_message: No active regular registration in another State under the same PAN.

conditions.description: No physical presence and no active regular registration in the target State.
conditions.fail_message: Applicant has a physical presence or regular registration in the target State.

conditions.description: Registration usable only for supplies through ECOs.
conditions.fail_message: Supplies in the target State are not limited to ECO supplies.

conditions.description: Output tax liability on supplies to registered persons within the monthly cap (config RULE14B-MONTHLY-CAP-LAKH).
conditions.fail_message: Expected monthly output tax on supplies to registered persons exceeds the Rule 14B cap.

conditions.description: Aadhaar authentication and document verification within 15 days of submitting Part B.
conditions.fail_message: Aadhaar authentication will not be completed.

routes.notes: R14A-NOT-25-6D is marked conflict because the handbook glosses s.25(6D) persons as "notified mandatory registrants", which does not match s.25(6D) (see conflict C-008). Whether a casual taxable person may opt for Rule 14A is not stated (UNVERIFIED).
routes.name: Rule 14A - simplified registration for small-liability taxpayers
routes.plain_language: If your monthly GST on sales to registered businesses stays within the cap and you complete Aadhaar authentication, a low-risk application can be approved electronically within 3 working days.

conditions.description: Applicant selects "Option for registration under Rule 14A = Yes".
conditions.fail_message: Applicant has not opted for Rule 14A.

conditions.description: Aadhaar authentication (OTP or biometric) of the authorised signatory and at least one promoter/partner; on the portal Rule 14A = Yes forces Aadhaar = Yes.
conditions.fail_message: Aadhaar authentication will not be completed, so Rule 14A is not available.

conditions.description: Applicant is not a person covered under s.25(6D) (Aadhaar-exempt classes under Notification 3/2021-CT).
conditions.fail_message: Applicant is in a class exempt from Aadhaar authentication under s.25(6D), so Rule 14A is not available.

conditions.description: No other Rule 14A registration on the same PAN in the same State/UT.
conditions.fail_message: A Rule 14A registration already exists (or is filed) on this PAN in this State.

conditions.description: Self-declared monthly output tax liability on supplies to registered persons within the cap (config RULE14A-MONTHLY-CAP-LAKH).
conditions.fail_message: Expected monthly output tax on supplies to registered persons exceeds the Rule 14A cap.

conditions.description: The "Input Service Distributor only" reason is disabled when Rule 14A = Yes.
conditions.fail_message: Rule 14A cannot be used for an Input Service Distributor registration.

routes.description: GSTN advisory of 1 Oct 2026 - normal taxpayers applying in two or more States/UTs under one PAN; common information auto-populated and editable per State.

source_ref.section: B. 1 Oct 2026 GSTN Advisory: Multistate Registration

routes.notes: Portal convenience, not a legal route. The GST tutorial also describes auto-population from an existing GSTIN on the same PAN.
routes.name: Multistate Registration facility on the portal
routes.plain_language: When applying in two or more States under one PAN, the portal can pre-fill common details for each State.

routes.description: Rules 8, 9 and 9A - REG-01 Part A (PAN, mobile, e-mail) then Part B; Aadhaar authentication or physical verification; Rule 9A electronic grant for low-risk cases.
routes.name: Normal registration
routes.plain_language: Apply on REG-01 on the GST portal. With Aadhaar authentication, a complete low-risk application is approved within 3 to 7 working days; otherwise allow up to 30 days for physical verification.

timelines.description: If the application is not submitted within 15 days, the TRN and all information against it are purged.
timelines.label: Complete Part B within 15 days of the TRN
timelines.plain_language: After Part A you get a Temporary Reference Number; finish and submit Part B within 15 days or the draft is deleted.

timelines.description: Rule 8(4A) - date of submission is the earlier of Aadhaar authentication or 15 days from submission of Part B.
timelines.label: Aadhaar authentication within 15 days of Part B
timelines.plain_language: The application counts as submitted on the earlier of Aadhaar authentication or 15 days after Part B, so authenticate quickly.

timelines.description: Rule 9A (Notification 18/2025-CT, from 1 Nov 2025) - applications categorised as low-risk by data analytics are approved by the portal within three working days; others follow Rule 9.
timelines.notes: The applicant cannot choose this; the portal decides.
timelines.label: Rule 9A: low-risk applications approved electronically within 3 working days
timelines.plain_language: If the portal's risk analysis rates your application low-risk, it is approved automatically within 3 working days.

timelines.description: Rule 9(1) and CBIC Instruction 03/2025-GST - officer approves within 7 working days of submission where not flagged risky and complete.
timelines.label: Rule 9: 7 working days for complete, non-risky applications
timelines.plain_language: Otherwise, a complete application not flagged as risky should be approved within 7 working days.

timelines.description: Rule 9(1) proviso and Rule 25 - physical verification of the principal place of business before grant, within 30 days of submission, report on REG-30 at least 5 working days before the period ends.
timelines.label: Up to 30 days where physical verification is needed
timelines.plain_language: If Aadhaar is not authenticated, the application is flagged risky, or the officer orders it, the premises are physically verified and approval can take up to 30 days.

timelines.description: Rule 9(2)-(4) - deficiency notice REG-03; clarification REG-04 within 7 working days; grant within 7 working days of satisfactory reply; rejection REG-05.
timelines.notes: Where physical verification applies, the notice can be issued within 30 days.
timelines.label: Query cycle: REG-03 within 7 working days, reply REG-04 within 7 working days
timelines.plain_language: If something is missing, the officer can raise one query within 7 working days; you have 7 working days to reply, and approval should follow within 7 working days of a satisfactory reply.

timelines.description: Rule 9(5) - deemed approval if no action within 7 working days (normal), 30 days (proviso cases) or 7 working days of the clarification.
timelines.label: Deemed approval if the officer does not act in time
timelines.plain_language: If the officer does nothing within these time limits, the registration is treated as approved.

timelines.description: Rule 10A - bank details within 30 days of grant or before GSTR-1/IFF, whichever is earlier; not applicable to Rule 12 (TDS/TCS) and Rule 16 (suo moto) registrants; default is ground for suspension (REG-31) and cancellation under Rule 21.
timelines.label: Bank account details within 30 days of grant
timelines.plain_language: After registration, add your bank account details within 30 days, or before filing your first GSTR-1/IFF if that is earlier, or the registration can be suspended.

timelines.description: Revised REG-01 (Advisory 681) - up to 10 bank accounts; unavailable details within 30 days of issue of REG-06.
timelines.label: Revised REG-01: up to 10 bank accounts; missing details within 30 days of REG-06
timelines.plain_language: On the new form you can give up to 10 bank accounts; any you cannot give now are due within 30 days of the registration certificate.

timelines.description: Rule 14A - after authentication, data analysis and risk evaluation; low-risk applications granted electronically within three working days; others processed under Rule 9 or 9A.
timelines.label: Rule 14A: electronic grant within 3 working days if low-risk
timelines.plain_language: After Aadhaar authentication, a low-risk Rule 14A application is approved within 3 working days; otherwise it goes through the normal process.

timelines.description: REG-32 withdrawal - all returns due filed; at least three months of returns if applying before 1 Apr 2026; no pending s.29 proceedings; order REG-33 or rejection REG-05.
timelines.notes: Contents of the GSTN advisory of 21 Feb 2026 on withdrawal not known (conflict C-003).
timelines.label: Leaving Rule 14A (before 1 Apr 2026): REG-32 after three months of returns
timelines.plain_language: To leave Rule 14A, file REG-32 after filing all returns due, with at least three months of returns filed and no cancellation proceedings pending.

timelines.description: REG-32 withdrawal - all returns due filed; at least one tax period's return if applying on or after 1 Apr 2026; no pending s.29 proceedings; liability above the cap only from the first day of the month after the REG-33 order.
timelines.notes: Contents of the GSTN advisory of 21 Feb 2026 on withdrawal not known (conflict C-003).
timelines.label: Leaving Rule 14A (from 1 Apr 2026): REG-32 after one tax period's return
timelines.plain_language: To leave Rule 14A, file REG-32 after filing all returns due (at least one tax period) with no cancellation proceedings pending. The higher liability applies from the month after the order.

timelines.description: Rule 14B - ECO consent within 7 working days.
timelines.label: Rule 14B: ECO consent within 7 working days
timelines.plain_language: Each marketplace must give its consent within 7 working days.

timelines.description: Rule 14B - Aadhaar authentication and document verification within 15 days of submitting Part B of REG-01.
timelines.label: Rule 14B: Aadhaar and document verification within 15 days of Part B
timelines.plain_language: Complete Aadhaar authentication and document verification within 15 days of submitting Part B.

timelines.description: Rule 14B - deemed approval on completion of the field visit or 30 days from ARN, whichever is earlier.
timelines.label: Rule 14B: deemed approval on field visit or 30 days from ARN
timelines.plain_language: Approval is treated as given when the field visit is completed or 30 days after the ARN, whichever is earlier.

timelines.description: Negative field-visit remarks may reject all pending Rule 14B applications linked to the same Home State GSTIN.
timelines.label: Rule 14B: a negative field visit can reject linked applications
timelines.plain_language: A bad field-visit report can reject all pending Rule 14B applications linked to the same home-State registration, so prepare premises evidence for each State.

timelines.description: Rule 12 - the proper officer may grant registration and issue REG-06 within 3 working days of submission.
timelines.notes: Rule 10A bank-details requirement does not apply to Rule 12 registrants.
timelines.label: REG-07: certificate within 3 working days
timelines.plain_language: TDS/TCS registrations are granted within 3 working days of the application.

timelines.description: Rule 8(6) - temporary reference number for advance deposit; REG-02 issued only after deposit; deposit is estimated net tax liability after eligible ITC (Circular 71/45/2018-GST).
timelines.label: Acknowledgement only after the advance deposit
timelines.plain_language: You get the acknowledgement (REG-02) only after paying the advance deposit of estimated net tax.

timelines.description: For NRTP, the ARN is generated only when payment of advance tax is done; acknowledgement REG-02 after deposit in the electronic cash ledger.
timelines.label: ARN only after the advance tax is paid
timelines.plain_language: The application reference number is generated only after the advance tax deposit is paid.

timelines.description: s.27(1), Rule 15(1) - validity for the period applied or 90 days, whichever earlier; extension up to 90 days on REG-11 with additional deposit.
timelines.label: Valid up to 90 days, extendable once by up to 90 days (REG-11)
timelines.plain_language: Your registration lasts up to 90 days; apply on REG-11 before expiry to extend it by up to 90 days, paying extra deposit.

timelines.description: Rule 14 - REG-06 granted subject to such conditions and restrictions and by such officer as notified; no time limit stated in the handbook.
timelines.label: No processing time stated
timelines.plain_language: The handbook does not state a processing time for REG-10; registration is granted subject to conditions notified by the Central Government.

documents.description: s.25(6) requires PAN for registration (except NRTP, s.25(7), and TDS deductors who use TAN).
documents.name: PAN of the business (or of the proprietor)
documents.detail: Every applicant must have a PAN. Legal name in the application must be exactly as in the PAN database; the constitution is validated against CBDT records.

documents.description: Proviso to s.25(6) - TDS deductor may obtain registration using TAN.
documents.name: TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number)
documents.detail: A person required to deduct tax under s.51 obtains registration using TAN instead of PAN.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, A(b) - partnership deed is the proof of constitution for partnership firms.
documents.notes: Instruction 03/2025-GST is dated 17.04.2025.
documents.name: Partnership deed
documents.detail: Upload the partnership deed as proof of constitution. Officers should not ask for Udyam/MSME, shop-establishment certificates or trade licences in addition.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, A(b) - registration certificate / proof of constitution.
documents.name: Registration certificate / proof of constitution
documents.detail: Society, trust, club, government department, AOP/BOI, local authority, statutory body and others upload their registration certificate or other proof of constitution.

documents.detail: The revised REG-01 validates LLPIN (FLLPIN for foreign LLPs) online and requires the DIN of designated partners.

documents.detail: Foreign company or entity - proof of incorporation and, where registered in India, FCRN.

documents.detail: Upload a photograph for each stakeholder entered in the Promoter/Partners tab (up to 10). Residential address and photograph are always entered manually.

documents.notes: The explicit list (letter or resolution with acceptance) appears in the NRTP section; applied generally. A proprietor signing personally needs no appointment proof (CA to confirm).
documents.name: Proof of appointment of authorised signatory
documents.detail: Letter of authorisation, or copy of the resolution of the Board of Directors / Managing Committee with an acceptance letter. PDF/JPEG up to 1 MB.

documents.description: Authorised Signatory tab - photograph (100 KB).
documents.name: Photograph of authorised signatory
documents.detail: Photograph of each authorised signatory, JPEG up to 100 KB.

documents.description: s.25(6B)/(6C), Rule 8(4A), Rule 9(1) proviso.
documents.notes: Exempt classes (Notification 3/2021-CT) - non-citizens, government departments, local authorities, statutory bodies, PSUs.
documents.name: Aadhaar authentication (OTP or biometric)
documents.detail: Proprietor / one partner / one director / Karta / a managing committee member, and the primary authorised signatory, authenticate Aadhaar through the link sent after submission. Opting out (or failing) means physical verification and up to 30 days. Biometric authentication at a GST Suvidha Kendra may be required if flagged, carrying originals of uploaded documents.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (i) Owned.
documents.name: Premises proof - owned: any ONE ownership document
documents.detail: Any one of - property tax receipt, municipal khata copy, electricity bill, or any other document under State or local law that clearly establishes the applicant's ownership. No additional ownership documents or originals should be sought.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (ii) Rented.
documents.notes: Rent/lease agreement upload up to 2 MB (handbook p. 99).
documents.name: Premises proof - rented, registered agreement
documents.detail: Valid rent/lease agreement plus any one ownership document of the lessor (as for owned premises). Identity proof of the lessor should NOT be sought. If the electricity or water connection is in the tenant's name, that document with the rent agreement is sufficient.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (ii) Rented - unregistered agreement.
documents.name: Premises proof - rented, unregistered agreement
documents.detail: Rent/lease agreement plus any one ownership document of the lessor, plus a copy of the lessor's identity proof. If the electricity or water connection is in the tenant's name, that document with the rent agreement is sufficient.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (vi) Rented/leased premises where agreement is not available.
documents.notes: No prescribed affidavit format in the handbook.
documents.name: Premises proof - rented, no agreement: affidavit
documents.detail: An affidavit to that effect on non-judicial stamp paper of the minimum value, executed before a First-Class Judicial Magistrate, Executive Magistrate or Notary Public, plus a document supporting possession, such as an electricity bill in the applicant's name.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (iii) not owned or rented (spouse, relative etc.).
documents.notes: From 26 Oct 2026 Circular 257 reportedly prescribes a consent-letter format (format not read).
documents.name: Premises proof - owned by spouse/relative etc.: consent letter
documents.detail: Consent letter on plain paper from the owner, a copy of the identity proof of the person giving consent, and any one ownership document of the owner.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (iv) Shared premises, agreement available.
documents.name: Premises proof - shared premises with agreement
documents.detail: Copy of the agreement plus any one ownership document. If the agreement is unregistered, add a copy of the lessor's identity proof; if registered, no identity proof of the lessor should be sought.

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (v) Shared premises, agreement not available.
documents.name: Premises proof - shared premises without agreement: consent letter
documents.detail: Consent letter on plain paper from the consenter, with the consenter's identity proof and any one document supporting the consenter's ownership (or other State/local-law document establishing ownership).

documents.description: Instruction 03/2025-GST, row (vii) PPOB in SEZ or applicant is SEZ developer.
documents.name: Premises proof - SEZ: Government of India approval documents
documents.detail: Necessary documents/certificates issued by the Government of India for the SEZ premises, uploaded as proof of SEZ unit/developer approval for the premises.

documents.description: Principal Place of Business tab - multiple documents uploaded as one file under "Others".
documents.notes: Revised REG-01 has standardised premises categories; treatment of "other" after 1 Nov 2026 NOT VERIFIED.
documents.name: Premises proof - other: legal ownership document (combined file)
documents.detail: Where several documents are needed, append them into a single file, choose "Others" as nature of possession and upload as the legal ownership document.

documents.notes: NOT VERIFIED.
documents.name: Premises proof - other (revised REG-01)

source_ref.section: C. Revised REG-01 - what to do differently

applicant_notes.text: For companies and LLPs, check that the legal name on PAN matches the MCA certificate before applying. From 1 Nov 2026 the CIN/LLPIN/FCRN/FLLPIN is validated online and a mismatch blocks the ARN.
Upload PDF or JPEG files. Most documents up to 1 MB; photographs up to 100 KB. If several documents prove one item, combine them into one file.

Officers are instructed to stick to the listed documents. They should not ask for originals, extra ownership proofs, or Udyam/MSME, shop-establishment or trade licences for partnerships. Any extra document needs Deputy/Assistant Commissioner approval.
If a REG-03 query asks for documents outside the prescribed list, reply citing Circular 257/03/2026-GST and keep a copy.
Aadhaar authentication decides whether you get the fast track. Without it, expect physical verification and up to 30 days.

applicant_notes.description: Place of business definition s.2(85); Illustration 7.
applicant_notes.text: Each additional place of business (branch, warehouse, godown) needs the same kind of premises proof as the principal place. Every warehouse from which you supply is a place of business.
The principal place of business is usually where the books of account are kept and senior management sits.
The SEZ unit or developer needs its own registration even if you are already registered in the same State outside the SEZ.

applicant_notes.description: Research note, revised REG-01 practical impact.

source_ref.section: C. Revised REG-01 - what to do differently

applicant_notes.text: Under the revised REG-01, complete the premises-possession and bank sections fully at the start. A validation failure now blocks the ARN instead of raising a query later.

If your monthly liability on sales to registered businesses may cross the Rule 14A cap, plan the exit (REG-32) before you need it. Higher liability is allowed only from the month after the withdrawal order.

source_ref.section: C. Rule 14B - what to do differently

applicant_notes.text: Do not file Rule 14B applications for several States in one batch without checking the premises evidence for each. A negative field visit can reject all linked applications.

applicant_notes.text: Add your bank account details on the GST portal within 30 days of getting your GSTIN, or before filing your first GSTR-1 / IFF if that is earlier. Otherwise the registration can be suspended.

applicant_notes.description: Illustration 1 - a registered person complies with all provisions.
applicant_notes.text: Once registered, voluntarily or compulsorily, you must charge GST on all your taxable sales and follow every rule that applies to a registered person.

applicant_notes.description: Illustration 2 - invoices before and after the effective date.
applicant_notes.text: GST applies only from the effective date of registration. Do not collect GST on invoices issued before it; invoices issued after the effective date but before you received the certificate are revised under section 31.
A casual or non-resident registration lasts up to 90 days. To continue, apply on REG-11 before it expires to extend it by up to 90 more days, with an extra advance deposit.
